02 / EVIDENCE & PROVENANCE

An experimental label,
with its context.

Different studies test different hosts, strains and conditions. The collection preserves those distinctions alongside each protein.

PHENOTYPE EVIDENCE

What was measured?

Records link identifiable protein-coding loci to genetic-perturbation experiments in roots, the rhizosphere or the endosphere. Each observation retains its assay, host and condition where available.

LABEL QUALIFICATION

Why this label?

Positive records follow reviewed source-specific perturbation evidence for a colonization deficit. Controls are tested, quality-qualified small-effect non-hits. Study-level rules and growth-control limitations remain visible in the evidence details.

SEQUENCE TRACEABILITY

Which native protein?

Gene and locus identifiers connect to complete native-strain proteins. Sequence hashes, mapping records and repaired homology-group identifiers support identity checks and reproducible data use.

04 / ABOUT & CITATION

A collection you can
inspect and reuse.

Experimental context and original source attribution are part of the database, from the first observation to the final protein record.

The manuscript collection

The formal dataset retains v0.12 sequences and labels with repaired V27 homology groups and frozen partition metadata. A protein can link to multiple source observations; studies and measurements are not additive unique-protein counts.

Control selection uses source-qualified finite effects within the recorded 0.8–1.2 point-effect band. This is an operational small-effect criterion rather than an equivalence test.

A separate H3 resource

Aquitalea magnusonii H3 was measured on duckweed surfaces. Its 1,878 proteins are provided separately as a historical surface-colonization transfer cohort and do not enter the 14,505-protein root-colonization collection.
